newsitem.title: USA: Female Health gets funds to boost production.
newsitem.headline: Female Health gets funds to boost production.

text.p: Female Health Co said Thursday it completed a previously announced plan to sell some real estate which will provide funds to increase production of its female condom.

The company said it completed the sale and a 20-year leaseback of a London manufacturing facility owned by its subsidiary, Chartex International. The transaction will eliminate $1.8 million in debt and provide $1.1 million to fund working capital requirements and for general corporate purposes.
The female condom is manufactured exclusively at the London facility, and Female Health will retain ownership of the facility's proprietary manufacturing equipment.
"We have been encouraged by orders for both the commercial and public sector markets," Female Health Chairman and Chief Executive Officer O.B. Parrish said in a statement.

Earlier this month, Female Health agreed to provide to a Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) global quantities of the product for distribution through UNAIDS. The company said that 80 countries have asked for more than seven million units. Funding is in place for more than half this order, and UNAIDS is currently assisting countries to finalize funding for the remainder, Female Health said.
Female Health owns the worldwide rights to the female condom including patents which have been issued in the U.S., Japan, The European Union, China, Canada, Brazil and Australia.
